approachQuestion.prompt:
Reverse the Announcement Order

A string announcement contains lowercase ASCII words separated by one or more ASCII spaces. Leading and trailing spaces are allowed. Return the words in reverse order, separated by exactly one space, with no leading or trailing space. Keep the character order within each word. If there are no words, return "".

Example 1: announcement="  doors   close now " → "now close doors".
Example 2: announcement="solo" → "solo".
Example 3: announcement="   " → "".

Constraints:
0 ≤ n=announcement.length ≤ 200,000. Only a–z and ASCII space occur.
Do not modify the input. Return a new flat string. Tabs and other whitespace do not occur.

options.text: Allocate a character buffer with n slots. Scan the original from right to left, skipping spaces and locating each word’s start and end. Copy each discovered word left to right into the next buffer positions, adding one space between words. Copy the used buffer prefix to the returned string.
options.feedback: Words are discovered in reverse order but their characters are copied forward. Skipping separators and adding one output separator normalizes spacing.

options.text: Copy announcement into a helper character array, then use the same right-to-left word-range scan to fill a separate n-slot buffer and copy its used prefix to the returned string.
options.feedback: This preserves all words and spacing rules, but the entire input copy is unnecessary because the original supports indexed reads.

options.text: Reverse all input characters and remove extra spaces, leaving the reversed characters within each word unchanged.
options.feedback: The order of characters inside words must stay intact. "open now" would become "won nepo", not "now open".

options.text: Scan from left to right, outputting each word and one space between consecutive words.
options.feedback: This normalizes spacing but fails to reverse words. "doors close" must become "close doors", not "doors close".

feedback.reason: Move backward to find the next word, but copy that word's characters forward.
details: Use a sized buffer. Move backward over spaces and then over each word to locate its boundaries. Copy that word forward into the buffer, separating output words with one space. Copy the occupied prefix into the returned flat string.

Move backward to find the next word, but copy that word's characters forward. Reversing the entire character stream would reverse letters inside words too. Separator normalization happens while writing, and an all-space input still requires scanning and the specified buffer allocation.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Discover Words Backward and Copy Them Forward”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the original length. Buffer allocation costs O(n+1). Indexed character reads/writes are constant time; copying an output of length L costs O(L+1), and L≤n. The buffer is distinct from the returned flat string because conversion copies it. Include buffer, indices and stack; exclude input and returned string. No recursion, hashing or dynamic append. Use a bound valid for n=0.
constraints: 0 ≤ n=announcement.length ≤ 200,000. Only a–z and ASCII space occur.
Do not modify the input. Return a new flat string. Tabs and other whitespace do not occur.

feedback.reason: Boundary discovery and character copying have linear total work.
details: Backward boundary discovery visits each original character at most once, and forward copying visits each output character once. Allocating n slots and copying the occupied prefix remain linear. The separate n-slot construction buffer is auxiliary storage.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: The two directions have linear total work and one separate buffer.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Excluding the returned string does not exclude its copied construction buffer.
The option “O((n + 1)²) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: Locating and copying disjoint words does not repeatedly rebuild previous output.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Even an all-space input must be scanned and the specified buffer allocated.
